question: For each score target: does an artefact upstream define the number, and can it be replayed here rather than transcribed?

classes.code: released evaluator code; replayed case by case against a pinned corpus
classes.rubric: machine-readable scoring data released without evaluator code; replayable as data
classes.prose: only a paper or a dataset README describes the number; the rule here is a transcription
classes.absent: the citation's own claim is that no scorer is published

upstream.entrypoint: evaluate(prediction: str, scoring_points: str) -> (passing, failing, score)

rows.cited: the RCA100 answer key, `answer_key/taxonomy.json`: `scoring_rubric` and a three-level fault hierarchy

probe.what: GET the raw file at the project path, twice: once as `AgenticOpsEval` (301) and once as `agenticopseval` (200)
probe.returned: a 25,823-byte JSON with `scoring_rubric`, `hierarchy` (L1_categories / L2_to_L1 / L3_to_L2) and `fault_definitions`

gap.summary: the fault-type term is binary here (`1` or `0`); the published rubric pays 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.2 for an exact L3, a shared L2 and a shared L1
gap.next: not a code change on its own: the rubric is 25 KB of CC BY-NC data that this project states it does not redistribute, so tiering needs either a licence decision (vendor it and apply it in the reader) or an offline fixture regenerated on demand. Measured again in finding 183: the fault type this exporter writes is a free-form IR string, so a tier would resolve only when the data already speaks RCA100 labels

rows.cited: the AIOps2025 dataset README, which describes the data and not the score; the formula is in the paper

probe.returned: no formula: the file documents the directory layout, the fault table and the citation. The only weight table found upstream is the project README, which states 0.40 / 0.40 / 0.10 / 0.10 and agrees with this repository

gap.summary: the LA relaxation is implemented; the second step of TA -- "embedding-similarity fallback for unhit cases" -- is not, because the section names neither a model nor a threshold
gap.evidence: arXiv 2606.29193v1 §4.4 :: "via two-step matching: keyword detection against the ground-truth fault descriptions (any hit yields full credit), with embedding-similarity fallback for unhit cases"
gap.next: a decision rather than a transcription: choosing a model changes the number, and choosing a threshold to reproduce the paper-reported TA would fit the metric to its own result. Recorded in golden-master/aiops2025-evaluator.json with the direction it costs

rows.metricSource: arXiv 2606.27154v2 section 3.2 (OpenRCA 2.0 outcome and process metrics)
rows.cited: arXiv 2606.27154v2 section 3.2 (outcome and process layers); no released scorer

probe.what: GET the tree of microsoft/OpenRCA at c121a483 and grep its README for `2.0` and `PAVE`; then fetch arXiv 2606.27154v2 and grep the flattened text for the metric definitions and for the string `open-sourced`
probe.returned: the repository has main/{evaluate.py, generate.py, prompt.py, task_specification.json} plus rca/, dataset/, docs/ -- 1.0 only, and neither `2.0` nor `PAVE` appears in its README. The paper defines the metric set in 3.2 (EM, F1/P/R over (service, fault_kind) pairs, AnySvc, Path Reachability, Node F1, Edge F1, SQL Exec) and `open-sourced` appears nowhere in it: the sentence this row used to quote was written in this repository

gap.summary: five of the nine published quantities are implemented (EM, AnySvc, PR, Node F1, Edge F1); PR uses the annotated path nodes as the alarm-node set, which makes it a lower bound rather than the paper number, F1/Precision/Recall collapse onto EM for a one-pair submission, SQL Exec needs queries, and MTTD needs per-attempt timestamps this contract does not carry
gap.evidence: arXiv 2606.27154v2 sec. 2.3 :: "A candidate path is verified only if all of (i) every node along it exhibits a deviation beyond its baseline screen" -- so the annotated path nodes are alarm nodes by construction, and PR needed no new field
gap.next: the lower bound closes one of two ways: the PAVE observation graph (which would name every deviating component, not only the ones on a surviving path), or a statement that G* is the alarm set by definition. Recorded in golden-master/openrca2-evaluator.json under alarmNodeBasis, with the direction of the error

rows.metricSource: arXiv 2502.05352 section 4.2 and table 3 (ITBench SRE diagnosis metrics; NTAM weights are tunable and unpublished, so the strict conjunction is this repository's own)
rows.cited: the ITBench paper; the repository ships scenarios and a deployment CLI

probe.what: GET the tree of IBM/itbench at b510385 and list src/, library/, schemas/, tests/, matching file names against /eval|scor|metric|judge|leaderboard/
probe.returned: src/itbench/{cli,models,utils} only -- commands to create, deploy and show scenarios. The two name matches are LEADERBOARD_{SRE,CISO}.md, which report NTAM and % resolved rather than pass@1

gap.summary: pass@1 is implemented as the paper defines it -- identifying the cause -- while the two NTAM metrics are not, because their contributions are tunable and the weights are not published
gap.evidence: arXiv 2502.05352v1 sec. 4.2 :: "Diagnosis efficiency is measured using pass@1(Chen et al., 2021) (i.e., identifying the cause as mentioned in ground truth), NTAM (Normalized Topology-Aware Metric) for root cause and fault propagation chain, and time to diagnosis"; and, on NTAM itself: "All the components have corresponding hyper-parameters that can be tuned to adjust their contributions to the overall score."
gap.next: a decision rather than a transcription: computing FL or FPC means choosing the weights the paper leaves tunable, and choosing them to reproduce a reported table would fit the metric to its own result. The strict conjunction this target reports is named as this repository's own in golden-master/itbench-evaluator.json, which also records the three of eight cases the old pass@1 rule called a failure and the paper calls a pass
